title: Shortest Honest Intervals for Individual-Effect Variance Bounds under Monotone Response
banked_reason: D0.5 math PASS; general referee graded the delivered analytic bracket incremental, below the fixed field floor (paper_score_ceiling 5.5 < 7.4; salvageable=false); exact connected-interval frontier and attaining rule remain open.
gap_reasons: The proposal headlined an exact computable connected-interval frontier with an attaining rule or sequence, but the theorem expressly delivers only a 17.384146--17.778047 bracket and leaves optimizer existence, interval-kernel approximation, and certified primal--dual convergence open.

The note proves a nontrivial analytic bracket and transfers its lower and upper witnesses, but it does not determine the shortest expected length, characterize an optimizer, or construct a sequence attaining R-star.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived an analytic bracket for the connected Gaussian interval value and transferred its lower bound and one anchored upper witness to the original multinomial experiment. The math referee passed those results, but the promised exact value, optimizer or attaining sequence, and certified interval-action approximation were not established. The general referee graded the delivered bracket incremental, below the field floor, and found no bounded repair in scope.
tldr: Average treatment effects conceal heterogeneity, while monotone response identifies only an ordered-transport upper bound on the variance of individual effects. At the specified five-score contact, that bound has local Gaussian target \(u_L-|u_B|\), and the pointwise connected-interval problem is non-equivariant. The rigorous headline is the analytic frontier bracket \(17.384146\leq R^{\star}\leq17.778047\): a residual two-ray Pratt argument proves the lower endpoint and an explicit globally honest anchored interval proves the upper endpoint. The same bracket transfers to the randomized trial through a universal local asymptotic lower bound and a data-only anchored interval. Exact Gaussian attainment, finite-cell density, a tight finite primal--dual certificate, and original-sample attainment of \(R^{\star}\) remain open.
gap: Directional optimal transport identifies the causal bound, and directional delta methods describe its non-Gaussian local limit, but the literature does not determine the shortest honest connected interval at a transport-dual tie. Classical expected-size theory either separates target values, uses unrestricted confidence regions, or assumes compact parameter spaces, leaving connected actions and the unbounded composite-fiber nuisance unresolved.
fill: The paper proves interval-kernel compactness and approximation, releases a finite certificate with width at most \(10^{-3}\), identifies an optimizer, transfers its constant through uniform multinomial LAN, and constructs an original-sample interval attaining the lower bound.
